modern: Let it make no difference to you whether you are cold or warm, if you are doing your duty; and whether you are drowsy or have had enough sleep; and whether spoken ill of or praised; and whether dying or doing something else. For it is one of the acts of life, this act by which we die; it is enough, then, in this act too, to do well what we have in hand.
original: Let it make no difference to thee whether thou art cold or warm, if thou art doing thy duty; and whether thou art drowsy or satisfied with sleep; and whether ill-spoken of or praised; and whether dying or doing something else. For it is one of the acts of life, this act by which we die; it is sufficient then in this act also to do well what we have in hand.

explained.summary:
When you’re doing what you should, the conditions don’t matter much: whether you’re cold or warm, tired or rested, criticised or praised. Marcus even adds dying to the list. Death is just one more thing we do in life, and like everything else, the task is simply to do it well when it comes.

The idea is to keep your attention on the job in front of you rather than on how comfortable or admired you feel while doing it.
explained.today: Think of finishing the report when you’re short on sleep, looking after a sick child on a freezing morning, or carrying on with a project after someone has rubbished it online. The tiredness and the criticism are real, but they don’t change what doing the work well looks like.
